rationale: No GCC state had announced an indefinite Iran trade embargo as of Aug 15; ACLED (Aug 4) and Irish Times (Aug 3) identify Bahrain and Kuwait as the most hostile toward Tehran (both struck Iran in July), while the UAE is re-opening trade, so an embargo, if any, is most likely from these two.

Treasury's Aug 5 action was a de-listing (Fly Baghdad) rather than a proxy designation update; amid the US-Iran war Treasury has consistently labeled Kataib Hezbollah and the Houthis as Iranian proxies, and a near-term August designation update is most plausible for Kataib Hezbollah.

German prosecutors indicted Serhii K. (aka Kuznietsov) on June 30 and he is already in Hamburg custody with trial due autumn (POLITICO/BBC July 1-2), while the second suspect was released by Poland in Oct 2025 and mastermind Roman Chervinsky is abroad; with only 16 days til Aug 19 a new arrest is unlikely, so 'None' stays high and any arrest most likely involves Serhii K.

Supreme Court fixed five petitions including the transfer-to-Shifa plea for Aug 18 (Express Tribune Aug 14), and Shifa is the hospital explicitly requested in Imran Khan's petition (Dawn Aug 1), but the court has repeatedly deferred on health matters so a PIMS-type government-facility order is a plausible alternative.
Interim governor Yeraldine Bonilla has held the post since May 2 and Rocha Moya's returns remain a personal decision with no FGR/US evidence yet (Infobae/El Informador Aug 11, Primera Nota Aug 13).

USS Abraham Lincoln has been on station off Iran for ~200+ days without a port call and is being relieved by USS George Washington (AP/CNN Aug 13-14); its next port call is most likely a Persian Gulf/logistics stop in the UAE or Bahrain, with a return home to the US (San Diego) a significant alternative.

AVROTROS will announce its 2027 decision in late August (NU.nl Aug 13, La Razón Aug 12) and has stayed silent since its Israel-related 2026 boycott; Ireland's RTÉ has been the most firmly opposed, while Spain and Slovenia have signaled open doors after EBU rule changes.

No 2026 Xi Middle East visit had occurred and none was announced as of Aug 15; China's most productive channel has been Saudi Arabia (phone call with MBS July 10, Wang Yi-Faisal talks) and post-war Iran diplomacy, with the Iran war making a Tehran trip plausible but uncertain.

The Bishkek SCO summit is Aug 31-Sept 1 (past the Aug 31 announcement deadline) and Indian reporting (Economic Times July 26) expects a Modi-Putin meeting where Ukraine would be on the agenda, making the Russian president's counterpart most likely Modi.

No Trump-proposed trilateral venue had surfaced as of Aug 15; Lavrov said Anchorage agreements had failed (July 24) and talks were stalled, with Gulf hubs (UAE, Saudi Arabia) and Turkey the most frequently floated neutral venues, followed by long-standing Swiss sites.

After Saudi Arabia's July 25 Houthi escalation and maritime coalition, the US and UK publicly called on Iran to stop supporting the Houthis (Arab News Aug 14), and Gulf mediators Qatar and Oman, along with China, are the states most likely to privately press Tehran via Reuters reporting.

Yemen's Coast Guard denied an Emirati landing attempt on Mayun in March and Saudi-linked Yemeni forces refused the UAE aircraft landing (Yemen Monitor Apr 3-8), indicating Saudi-backed Tareq Saleh government forces control the island, though Houthi takeover amid the renewed war is a real risk.
